walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme B: Religion & Life — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme B: Religion & Life brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme B: Religion & Life.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
The Eightfold Path is eight gods Buddhists must please.
Christians believe in three different gods.

mcqs.q: What is the Eightfold Path in Buddhism?
options: The Eightfold Path is the same as the Four Noble Truths.
The Eightfold Path is eight gods Buddhists must please.
Atonement means Jesus apologised to humans for being born divine.

The practical path to ending suffering: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration — grouped into wisdom, ethical conduct and mental discipline.

mcqs.q: What are the main Christian theories of atonement?
options: The Eightfold Path is eight gods Buddhists must please.

Penal substitution (Christ bore the punishment for sin), Christus Victor (Christ defeated evil powers through the cross), ransom theory (Christ paid a price to free humanity), and moral exemplar (Christ's death inspires love). Different traditions emphasise different theories.
All Christians believe Jesus died only to pay God back for sin.
Atonement means Jesus apologised to humans for being born divine.
